limits_arithmetic.ceiling_crosscheck: Wall: A 600≤900, B 600≤600, C 900≤1200, E 120≤120, F 2700≤2700. Memory: A/B/C/E 2 GiB≤2 GiB, F 8 GiB≤8 GiB. Pids: B 128≤256, E 128≤256, F 1024≤1024. Source: B/E 1287098368≤1287099500. Packet: C 67108864≤67108864. Target/tmp: F 8589934592≤21474836480. Logs: all ≤16777216. Every value is a positive int. Every memory value is a 4096 multiple, so the memory.max readback equals what was written.
limits_arithmetic.fixed_mount_consistency: quotas() requires mount max_bytes ≤ phase allowance in every phase. Every phase therefore carries exactly source_bytes=1287098368, target_tmp_bytes=8589934592 and packet_bytes=67108864, equal to the three fixed mounts.
limits_arithmetic.source: 1287098368 = 314233×4096, the page floor of the 1287099500 ceiling, so statvfs f_blocks×f_frsize equals it exactly. Headroom over the predicted 1029679600 logical bytes is 257418768. At an average 2048 B page-rounding loss per file, that covers about 125k files. The file count is unobserved.
limits_arithmetic.target_tmp: 8 GiB, below the 20 GiB ceiling. F is the only large writer, and its writes are charged to F memory.max = 8 GiB anyway (see memory_accounting), so a larger tmpfs adds no usable room.
limits_arithmetic.packet_and_logs: Packet is 64 MiB, forced by the C ceiling. The log caps apply cumulatively per phase across variants. stdout totals 18 MiB and stderr 11 MiB, so the worst case is 29 MiB = 30408704 B. That leaves 36700160 B for receipts and results. With 16 MiB caps the worst case would be 224 MiB, and packet ENOSPC would preempt the clean log cap.
limits_arithmetic.cpu_time: cpu_time_us = wall × quota/period × 1e6. It equals the hard rate bound, so it is a consistent explicit cap, not a tighter one.
limits_arithmetic.E: Within 120 s at 1 CPU, E runs two full ~910 MB re-identity hash passes (precheck plus audit), about 1.82 GB, and cargo metadata. That needs at least 18.2 MB/s effective hashing if metadata takes 20 s. Not observed.
limits_arithmetic.total_wall_seconds: 6720 = phase sum 300+600+600+900+600+120+2700 = 5820, plus a 900 s inter-phase supervisor margin. The margin covers up to 30 full passes (25 expected) at about 30 s each for bound_identities/quotas/receipts.
limits_arithmetic.supervisor_cpu_seconds: 10800. run() sets RLIMIT_CPU on the supervisor before any fork, and join_child does not reset it, so every phase process inherits it per process. A lower value could SIGXCPU-kill a single multithreaded rustc in F (up to 2700 s × 4 CPUs = 10800 s). The supervisor itself is effectively bounded by min(10800, leaf cpu.max 1 CPU × 6720 s) = 6720 CPU-s.
limits_arithmetic.file_bytes: Workers: 64 MiB, since nothing larger fits the packet and the largest staged git db file is ≤ 21866070. B: 256 MiB per extracted file. F: 4 GiB, enough for a debug test binary and still inside the F memcg.
limits_arithmetic.namespace_tmpfs_bytes: 16 MiB for workers, B and E; 64 MiB for F. Charged inside the phase memcg. The consumer is in sandbox_args, which is not supplied (see reading_limits).

cgroup_operator_contract.E: /sys/fs/cgroup/moriarty-a102-compile-r1: a top-level cgroup outside systemd units. Created by a root operator, dir root:root 0755. memory.max=21474836480, memory.swap.max=0, pids.max=1088, cpu.max='500000 100000', cgroup.subtree_control='+cpu +memory +pids'. All files stay root:root 0644 except cgroup.procs, which is chowned 1000:1000. That is the only supervisor-writable E file, and it serves as the migration common ancestor. E holds no processes; its only children are supervisor and phases.
cgroup_operator_contract.L: E/supervisor: root:root 0755, all files root-owned. memory.max=1610612736, memory.swap.max=0, pids.max=64, cpu.max='100000 100000'. subtree_control is empty and there are no children. These values are set by the operator; the runner does not check them.
cgroup_operator_contract.P: E/phases: created by root with memory.max=18534076416, memory.swap.max=0, pids.max=1024, cpu.max='400000 100000' and cgroup.subtree_control='+cpu +memory +pids', all set before delegation. Then chown 1000:1000 on the P directory, P/cgroup.procs, P/cgroup.threads and P/cgroup.subtree_control only. P resource files stay root-owned, so the supervisor cannot raise them. The runner creates the phase children itself.
cgroup_operator_contract.constraints: uid 1000 owns nothing at or above E except E/cgroup.procs and cannot write any E/L/P cap. Escape out of E needs write on a root-owned ancestor's cgroup.procs, which is denied. Entering E's internal node fails because controllers are enabled (no-internal-process rule). The supervisor must have CapPrm/CapEff/CapAmb = 0, uid = euid = 1000, and /proc/self/cgroup exactly '0::/moriarty-a102-compile-r1/supervisor'. No agent ever holds root; a human operator performs every root step.
cgroup_operator_contract.host_predicates_OBSERVATION_REQUIRED: Exactly one cgroup2 mount at /sys/fs/cgroup and no mount beneath it. /proc/self/cgroup is a single line. /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control contains cpu, memory and pids. cgroup.kill is present. A WSL2 hybrid layout would fail supervisor_envelope; this assistant's session reports a WSL2 kernel, and whether that is the execution host is unobserved.

memory_accounting.principle: tmpfs pages, plus inode and dentry kernel memory, are charged to the writing task's memcg. With swap.max = 0 they cannot be reclaimed. Charges from removed phase cgroups stay counted under P and E until teardown frees the pages. Page cache from read-only binds is charged to the reader and is reclaimable. Namespace tmpfs is charged inside each phase. This is general kernel semantics, not observed on this kernel.
memory_accounting.arithmetic: tmpfs 1287098368 + 8589934592 + 67108864 = 9944141824. Add F 8589934592, supervisor 536870912 and margin 1073741824: total 20144689152. This double-counts F's own tmpfs writes, so it is conservative. Envelope 21474836480 leaves 1330147328 slack. P 18534076416 = tmpfs total + F, and L 1610612736 = supervisor + margin, so P + L = 20144689152 ≤ E. Envelope OOM therefore cannot pre-empt a phase cap. Pids: 1088 = P 1024 + L 64. CPU: E 5 = P 4 + L 1.
memory_accounting.F_effective_target_capacity: At most 8589934592 minus peak F process RSS (-j4) minus F tmp and namespace-tmpfs writes. Debug test-build target size is unobserved. Exceeding it is a cgroup OOM, which is terminal. This is the most likely resource failure, and only a source change to the 8 GiB owner ceiling could remove it; that is out of scope.
memory_accounting.host_capacity: UNOBSERVED. No assumption is made. The OP-0 gate is MemAvailable ≥ 23622320128. Fewer than 4 online CPUs is a wall-cap risk only, not a safety risk.
